_source: AI-researched venue CANDIDATES for Manchester and Cheshire, awaiting review — never directly edited by the research agent. Populated by a daily scheduled research agent (2026-08, at explicit user request: 'fan out some research agents who's goal is to run every day to find and suggest new businesses... they shouldn't go beyond cheshire and manchester just yet'; bumped from ~3-5/day to 10/day at a later explicit request). See .claude/agents/curia-research-daily.md for the full research brief/rules this agent works under (Hard rule 1 chain/fast-food screening, real coordinates only, no duplicates, Do/Drink/Eat coverage balance). The research agent commits straight to master for this file (no PR — this queue has zero effect on the live app, nothing reads it except the review agent and the admin dashboard's Growth Insights context). A second, independent daily agent (.claude/agents/curia-suggestion-review.md) re-verifies each `pending` entry and is the thing that promotes one into the real docs/data/venues.json, pushing straight to master after its own independent re-verification (see that file's own 2026-09-04 doc comment for why the human checkpoint moved to Curia Command's Pending Review tab instead of a PR here). Each entry mirrors docs/data/venues.json's own raw shape (name/district/type/spend/lat/lon/base/bands/reason) exactly, so a reviewed-and-approved entry can be moved into that file with a straight copy-paste, plus review-only fields (suggestedDate, status, researchNotes) that get stripped on promotion. `district` values must be a real existing district id from docs/data/districts.json (manchester/cheshire metros only) UNLESS the entry is itself proposing a brand-new district — see district-suggestions.json for that case instead; a venue suggestion should never invent a district id that doesn't exist anywhere.
_reviewWorkflow: status starts 'pending' on every new entry. The daily curia-suggestion-review agent changes it to 'approved'/promoted (then copies the venue fields into docs/data/venues.json and removes the entry here, pushed straight to master) or 'rejected' (left here with researchNotes explaining why, as a record so the same candidate isn't re-suggested later — curia-research-daily checks every entry here regardless of status before suggesting anything new). Genuinely uncertain candidates go to docs/data/pending-review-queue.json instead, staying 'pending' here until a human decides via Curia Command. A human's actual review happens by reading Curia Command's daily briefing and Pending Review tab, not by editing this file directly, though a human reviewer (or a future admin-dashboard screen) can still hand-edit an entry's status here if needed.

suggestions.name: Clark Art
suggestions.reason: Bill Clark's own gallery on Ashley Road since 1999, deep in L.S. Lowry and the northern painters he's written the books on — a private dealer's eye, not a gallery chain's algorithm.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Clark Art (155 Ashley Road, Hale) closed permanently on 3 October 2024 after 18 years, per Bill Clark's own retirement announcement (reported by Altrincham Today, 'An incredible journey: Clark Art to close after 18 years in Hale village'). The prior research pass's sources (Tripadvisor/Artsy/halebarns.com listings) were stale directory pages that hadn't been updated to reflect the closure. Do not re-suggest — the gallery no longer exists.

suggestions.name: Yang Sing
suggestions.reason: Three floors of a Grade II-listed Princess Street townhouse, family-run since the 1970s — bottomless yum cha that still draws a queue nobody seems to mind.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Yang Sing (34 Princess Street) has been closed since December 2021/early 2022 (kitchen fire, then a lease dispute) and Yang Sing Limited is now in liquidation per Companies House — it never reopened despite the owner's 2022 hope to reopen by 2023/24. The prior research pass's sources (visitmanchester.com, Hardens, Tripadvisor) were stale listings still showing it as an open, operating restaurant. Do not re-suggest unless it demonstrably reopens under new ownership.

suggestions.name: Blue Lobster
suggestions.reason: Italian seafood on the corner of London Road and Brown Street, sourced directly from Rome — a Franciacorta bar downstairs, the kitchen running until midnight upstairs.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Blue Lobster (34 London Road, Alderley Edge) closed permanently in December 2017, less than nine months after its April 2017 opening, following a staff-payment dispute with owner Andrea Zecchino (reported by alderleyedge.com and Manchester Confidential at the time). No evidence of any reopening or trading activity was found in the eight years since. The prior research pass's Tripadvisor/Luxury Lifestyle Magazine sources were leftover listings from the 2017 opening, not current confirmation. Do not re-suggest unless it demonstrably reopens under new ownership.

suggestions.name: Fire Station Social Cucina
suggestions.reason: A pizza theatre and wood oven where Gusto used to sit on London Road — hand-rolled pasta, Napoli-style bases, and only one other room anywhere doing the same thing.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via thebusinessdesk.com, wilmslow.co.uk/alderleyedge.com and the operator's own site (firestationsocial.co.uk): Fire Station Social Cucina, 75 London Road, Alderley Edge SK9 7DY, opened 10 June 2026 in the former Gusto unit — the second site for this specific concept, after the original in Tarporley. Run by 'Project Social Cucina', the restaurant division of Cheshire Pub Company (a separate entity from the 7-pub Cheshire Cat group already referenced elsewhere in this file) — only 2 sites confirmed under the Fire Station Social Cucina name itself, the same 2-site sibling precedent already used for Cibo/Suburban Green/Smoke Wilmslow/Heddy's/Caramello. Flagged for the reviewer: the parent company's own press describes this as 'expansion', so worth a quick re-check at promotion time that a third site hasn't since appeared. Moderate-high confidence otherwise — real, recently opened, well-covered locally, no closure signals. Re-checked again 2026-09-08 (curia-suggestion-review daily pass) specifically for a rumoured third site: none found — same 2-site status as this note originally recorded, still pending, still in docs/data/pending-review-queue.json for a human call rather than re-decided here. DECIDED 2026-09-08 by direct user instruction, in an interactive session: promoted into venues.json with the new `status: 'coming-soon'` field (added the same day specifically for this case) rather than a flat yes/no — real venue, passes Hard rule 1 on site count today, but its editorial confidence marker stays provisional given the parent's stated expansion plans. See venues.json's own note on the new field.

suggestions.name: The Copper Room
suggestions.reason: Amy and Rick Armstrong crowdfunded their way into Charles Roe House's Grade II* rooms — steak and seafood cooked properly, in a silk merchant's own dining room on Chestergate.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via the operator's own site (chefrick.co.uk), Macclesfield Nub News (two separate pieces confirming both the Kickstarter-funded opening and the venue name) and Tripadvisor (active listing with 2026-dated reviews): The Copper Room, Charles Roe House, 60-62 Chestergate, Macclesfield SK11 6DY, a fine-dining restaurant and cocktail bar run by chef-owners Amy and Rick Armstrong. No second site or group ownership found anywhere — single-site, independently owned, passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Coordinates from doogal.co.uk's postcode geocode for SK11 6DY. Reuses the existing FINE DINING type. Fills a real gap: Macclesfield had only 1 Eat-category venue (Chestergate Bistro) against 2 Do and 3 Drink before this addition. REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-14: the chef-owned fine-dining concept this candidate described no longer trades at 60-62 Chestergate. Charles Roe House's dining room changed to 'Piccante at The Copper Room' (Italian/Brazilian tapas, opened Dec 2022) and per Macclesfield Nub News that room has sat empty since summer 2025 while the building is converted into a different, unrelated venture, 'The Charles Roe Pub' (reopening Dec 2025). Amy and Rick Armstrong's ownership story checks out, but whatever they run today is not trading at this address under this description — a closure/identity mismatch, not a chain issue. Do not re-suggest at this address; a genuinely reopened Armstrong-run venue elsewhere would need its own fresh verification.

suggestions.name: Prana
suggestions.reason: Two floors of proper acoustics on Ashley Road from the team behind Stockport's Amp — order the cocktail, but the stage is the reason to stay past nine.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-22: Google Maps marks it 'Permanently closed' (posting disabled), its own site returns a dead Cloudflare error, Instagram/Facebook are gone, Skiddle shows zero events ever listed, and its sister venue (Amp, Stockport) also closed and reopened under an unrelated name/concept. The property itself (14-16 Ashley Road) is listed for sale as former restaurant premises. Companies House shows an 'Active' shell (PRANA F&B LIMITED) with overdue first accounts — not evidence of an operating business. Do not re-suggest.

suggestions.name: Mouro Coffee Bar
suggestions.reason: Moroccan tile underfoot and a La Marzocco machine doing the actual work — focaccia sandwiches, matcha and affogato for a stretch of Heaton Moor Road that doesn't need to shout about any of it.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via Tripadvisor (5.0/5, current 2026 listing), the Food Standards Agency ratings register and the venue's own Instagram (@mourocoffeebar): Mouro Coffee Bar, 72 Heaton Moor Road, Stockport SK4 4NZ — a design-led independent coffee bar serving speciality coffee, cold-pressed juices, pastries and focaccia sandwiches. No second site or group ownership found anywhere despite a direct search; single-site, passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Coordinates from postcode geocode for SK4 4NZ. Reuses the existing BRUNCH SPOT type. Heaton Moor was at 8 venues (3 Do, 3 Drink, 2 Eat) before this addition — Eat was its thinnest category, and the district is one of ten currently under the 10-venue standing target. High confidence. REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-16: the 'no second site found anywhere' claim doesn't hold up — Mouro is in fact a real, actively expanding four-site coffee brand: the original Heaton Moor site, two Altrincham sites (25 Market Street and 8-10 Oxford Road, opened August 2025), and a fourth opened 16 May 2026 on Tib Street in the Northern Quarter itself (themanc.com's own coverage explicitly headlines it 'Mouro opens third coffee shop', undercounting even by its own count since two Altrincham sites exist). This is well past this file's established 2-3-site small-sibling-group allowance and spans two separate towns plus a city-centre expansion — a real, currently-growing chain by Hard rule 1's own standard, not a family pair. Do not re-suggest unless the brand's footprint materially contracts.

suggestions.name: Underbank
suggestions.reason: A former bank branch turned beer hall and soundsystem room at the crossroads of the two Underbanks — Pomona Island and Runaway on tap, and a rig loud enough that conversation moves to the beer garden after ten.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-22: investigated as a suspected name/identity mismatch with the existing 'The Underbank' catalog entry (same building, 27 Great Underbank). Found no evidence a second real venue exists — the theory traced to a January 2025 Instagram announcement (Benji Taylor's own plan for a live-music venue in the same building) that appears to have been superseded by what actually opened in May 2025 (the O'Malleys' 'The Underbank', which itself runs gigs/comedy/quiz nights, not just a beer hall). The existing catalog entry's name and core facts are correct as-is. Do not re-suggest as a separate venue without direct on-the-ground confirmation.

suggestions.name: Olive Tree Brasserie
suggestions.reason: Meze and a bottomless brunch on Watergate Row since 2016 — Dean Wilson's third room, not his first draft, and it still runs on a Greek kitchen's own instincts.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-22: the original candidate's '3rd site, Lytham/Preston/Chester' framing understated the real scale — the group's own site today lists FOUR active locations (Chester, Leeds, Lytham, Stockton Heath) across three counties, plus a closed 5th site (Preston, liquidated 2021). Founder/director Dean Wilson was disqualified from running any company for 10.5 years in Nov 2024 after fraudulently claiming ~£200k in COVID Bounce Back Loans across the group's per-site companies. A genuine multi-city regional chain, not a small group — do not re-suggest.

suggestions.name: Bali Health Lounge
suggestions.reason: Three floors above George Street built around ELEMIS facials and a tea lounge — Chinatown's actual quiet room, one flight up from everything loud below it.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-22, overturning an earlier 'moderate-high confidence, still trading' read: the operating company (Bali Health Lounge Limited, #07411581, same address) passed a creditors' voluntary liquidation resolution in Dec 2022 and was formally dissolved 4 Dec 2024 (The Gazette, Companies House). The 'live' Yelp/Tripadvisor activity that misled the earlier pass is uncurated listing pages carrying stale marketing copy with auto-generated 'Updated' headers regardless of actual status — no genuinely-dated 2023-2026 review or evidence of a relaunch was found. Do not re-suggest unless a new operator/relaunch is confirmed.

suggestions.name: The Nest Nantwich
suggestions.reason: Nick Wadeson's own copper still, Valerie, still runs on Pepper Street — the family behind Three Wrens Gin poured their production room into a proper cocktail bar rather than settling for a tasting counter.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED — exact duplicate of a venue already live in docs/data/venues.json under the identical name and coordinates (a different real venue on Pepper Street, Nantwich, already catalogued as a cocktail bar with its own working still). The pipeline's dedup logic only checks this suggestions file, not venues.json itself, so it missed the collision. Do not re-suggest.

suggestions.name: Amici
suggestions.reason: Italian-Greek tapas in the Village Square, run by Andrea, Giovanni and Chris on a menu that never quite picks a country — steak and seafood mains for whoever wants to stop sharing.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED — exact duplicate of a venue already live in docs/data/venues.json under the identical name, district and coordinates (Bramhall, Italian-Greek tapas, Andrea/Giovanni/Chris). Same dedup gap as The Nest Nantwich/Amazing India in this same batch. Do not re-suggest.

suggestions.name: Amazing India
suggestions.reason: Joby Joy's South Indian room on Pickford Street, the only one of its kind in town — dosas and a party hall that means the celebration doesn't have to end when the curry does.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED — exact duplicate of a venue already live in docs/data/venues.json under the identical name, district and near-identical coordinates (Macclesfield, South Indian, Pickford Street). Same dedup gap as The Nest Nantwich/Amici in this same batch. Do not re-suggest.

suggestions.name: King Street Kitchen
suggestions.reason: Small, family-run, and on King Street since long before the brunch queue started forming outside it — a plant-based option on every course, not just the one everyone else bothers with.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED — this venue was already investigated, confirmed closed (two independent listing sites marking it CLOSED, corroborated by a local Facebook post) and removed from docs/data/venues.json on 2026-09-08 (see docs/data/pending-review-queue.json's own record of that decision). The daily research pipeline re-suggested it again on 2026-09-22 without checking that history — a real dedup gap (this file's own dedup logic only checks entries within this file, not venues.json's removal/closure history). Do not re-suggest; if the pipeline's dedup logic gets fixed, this is the case that should have caught it.

suggestions.name: Coco Tang
suggestions.reason: Eighteen years of running Nottingham's Byard Lane before Manchester got a look — Vietnamese café by day, a cocktail room and late kitchen once the Bridge Street lights come on.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via restaurantonline.co.uk and premierconstructionnews.com's own coverage of the Manchester opening, plus Tripadvisor/Instagram for the original Nottingham site: Coco Tang, taking over the former SakkuSamba/Artisan unit at 1 The Avenue, Bridge Street, Spinningfields, opening autumn 2026 — an independent Vietnamese café, restaurant, private dining space and late-night cocktail bar/club, run by the same owners as the 18-year-old original Coco Tang in Nottingham (Byard Lane). A real 2-site pair across two cities, industry press explicitly describing it as 'independent' rather than a chain expansion — within the same 'single sibling in another city' precedent already established in this file (e.g. Craig's, Ivy Spinningfields). No third site found. District placement: industry coverage explicitly calls the address 'Spinningfields'/'Bridge Street in Spinningfields' despite 1 The Avenue sitting right at the Deansgate boundary; coordinates approximated from the John Rylands Library/1 The Avenue building's known location (postcode-geocoding blocked this session) since the exact unit number wasn't published at time of writing — flagged for the reviewer to tighten once the venue is trading and a precise address is published. Reuses the existing VIETNAMESE type. Spinningfields' real Eat category (Celebratory, Fine Dining, Small Plates) was its thinnest before this addition. Moderate-high confidence — the venue and ownership are well-documented; the exact coordinate and the opening date (announced, not yet independently confirmed as trading) are the flagged caveats.

suggestions.name: Stile Napoletano
suggestions.reason: Giacomo's dough gets its own slow Neapolitan ferment on Watergate Street — one of Europe's fifty best pizzerias by outside reckoning, and still just the one room to prove it in.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via the operator's own site (stilenapoletanopizzeria.co.uk), Tripadvisor (current, active listing) and visitcheshire.com: Stile Napoletano, 49 Watergate Street, Chester CH1 2LB — an independent Neapolitan pizzeria, listed among Europe's top 50 pizza restaurants per multiple press mentions. No second site found anywhere in searches for the name; single-site, passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Coordinates (53.1898/-2.8936) from britishlistedbuildings.co.uk's own geocode for the 49 Watergate Street building itself, not a district centroid. Reuses the existing PIZZERIA type (Pix Pizza, Rudy's). Closes Chester's most acute real gap found this run: only 2 Eat-category venues (Paysan, Shrub) against 5 Do venues before this addition. High confidence — well-documented, single-site, no closure signals.

suggestions.name: Chez Jules
suggestions.reason: Rustic French cooking in Chester's old fire station since 1997 — steak frites and a wine list that has never once chased a trend to stay full.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via the operator's own site (chezjules.com), Yelp (21 reviews, active 2026 listing) and chester360.co.uk: Chez Jules, 71 Northgate Street, Chester CH1 2HQ, in the city's former fire station — trading since 1997, described consistently as Chester's only independent French restaurant. No second site found anywhere in searches. Coordinates (53.193451/-2.893359) from Apple Maps' own place geocode for this exact address. Reuses the existing FRENCH BISTRO type (Paysan, also in Chester — a second, distinct French room is a real and reasonable overlap, not a duplicate). Second of two candidates closing Chester's acute Eat gap this run. High confidence — 29 years of continuous trading, no closure signals found.

suggestions.name: Barlounge
suggestions.reason: Twenty-five years on Watergate Street and only just reimagined this February — Chester's actual late room, not a hotel bar playing at being one.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via thecheshiremagazine.co.uk ('Spotlight On: Barlounge, Chester'), thechesterblog.com (Feb 2026 'Reimagined Barlounge now open' piece confirming current trading) and chesterbid.co.uk: Barlounge, 75 Watergate Street, Chester CH1 2LB, opened 2000 by Neil McDonnell (later joined by Jason Bligh), celebrating 25 years as an independent Chester bar and restaurant. No second Barlounge site found anywhere in searches — single-site, passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Coordinates extrapolated from britishlistedbuildings.co.uk's geocode for the nearby 73 Watergate Street building (53.1896/-2.8946), since 75 itself wasn't individually listed — flagged for the reviewer to tighten if an exact geocode becomes available, but both buildings sit on the same short block. Reuses the existing COCKTAIL BAR type — the district currently has no venue mapped to the 'Cocktail bars' onboarding tile at all despite three Drink-adjacent venues (Huxley's wine bar, Craft & Company gin bar, Beer Heroes bottle shop), a real tile-coverage gap this closes. High confidence — long-established, independently confirmed still trading via a Feb 2026 refurbishment reopening, not just stale listing pages.

suggestions.name: Thom's Bar & Kitchen
suggestions.reason: Thom Collins runs the wine and cocktail list, his parents run the room — a family concern on Heaton Moor Road that's never needed a rebrand to stay full.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via Stockport Council's own planning register (DC070486, 'Thom's Wine Bar and Restaurant at the Orangery, 54 Heaton Moor Road'), squaremeal.co.uk and Facebook (@ThomsBarHM, current 2026 activity): Thom's Bar & Kitchen (trading name variously as Thom's Wine Bar & Restaurant / Thom's Bar & Kitchen), 54 Heaton Moor Road, Stockport SK4 4NZ — owned and run by Thom Collins with his parents Derek and Sally, long-time Heatons residents. No second site found anywhere in searches; single-site, passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Coordinates from the SK4 4NZ postcode centroid (53.4235/-2.1833) — same street as the district's existing Cork of the North wine bar, a few doors along. Reuses the existing WINE BAR type. Heaton Moor's Drink category (Heaton Social, Cork of the North) was its thinnest before this addition, once Beer Shop (a bottle shop, not a bar) is set aside. Moderate-high confidence — well-documented, family-run, no closure signals; note this is a different venue from the previously-rejected 'Mouro Coffee Bar' candidate at a different number on the same road (that one failed on an unrelated multi-site chain finding).

suggestions.name: Little Tap
suggestions.reason: A former butcher's shop turned craft beer and cocktail den on Tarporley's high street — Myles Carr split the kitchen off across the road once the bar itself got too busy to also cook.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via CAMRA/whatpub.com, the Chester and District Standard's own coverage of the owner's second site, and the operator's own site (littletaptarporley.co.uk): Little Tap, 69 High Street, Tarporley CW6 0DP — opened 2016 in a former butcher's shop, owner Myles Carr, serving craft beer, wine, cocktails and gin. Myles opened a second site, Terrarium by Little Tap, directly across the road in 2024 to separate the food side of the business — a real 2-site pair, both in the same village under one owner, a smaller and less risky version of the 'single sibling elsewhere' precedent already accepted in this file (Craig's, Ivy Spinningfields, Fire Station Social Cucina). No third site found. Coordinates from the CW6 0DP postcode centroid, verified via postcodes.io-derived search — note this postcode sits close to, but is distinct from, the CW6 0DX postcode used for the Tarporley district centroid itself. Reuses the existing COCKTAIL BAR type. Tarporley's Drink category (The Swan gastropub, Piste Wine Bar, Bonjour Wines merchant) was its thinnest before this addition. High confidence — long-established, well-documented, no closure signals.

suggestions.name: RedWillow
suggestions.reason: Macclesfield's own brewery pouring straight from the tank on Park Green — five cask lines, fifteen keg, and nothing on them that was brewed anywhere but the Lodge up at Sutton Garrison.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via CAMRA (brewery listing), pintpoint.co.uk (live, current tap list) and the brewery's own site (redwillowbrewery.com/pages/macclesfield): RedWillow, 32a Park Green, Macclesfield SK11 6TN — the taproom for RedWillow Brewery (production site at The Lodge, Sutton Garrison, Byrons Lane). RedWillow runs one other bar, in Buxton, Derbyshire — flagged for the reviewer as a 2-site pair across two towns, the same small-sibling-group scale already accepted elsewhere in this file (e.g. Fire Station Social Cucina's 2 sites), not a wider chain. Coordinates approximated from a nearby Park Green building's geocode (59 Park Green, SK11 7NH: 53.255591/-2.122718) since 32a itself wasn't individually listed — same street, flagged for the reviewer to tighten if a precise geocode becomes available. Reuses the existing BREWERY TAP type (see tile-catalog-map.ts's 2026-09-22 note introducing it). Macclesfield's Drink category was its thinnest alongside Eat before this addition. Moderate-high confidence — well-documented, currently pouring per live tap-list sources; the Buxton sibling is the one flag worth a second look at promotion time.

suggestions.name: Serenity Booksellers
suggestions.reason: A family-run shop of books, gifts and local art a few minutes off the Market Place — wide aisles, and nothing on the shelves an algorithm put there.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via manchestercityofliterature.com, nationalbooktokens.com's own stockist listing and Facebook (current 2026 posts): Serenity Booksellers, 11 Warren Street, Stockport SK1 1UD — a family-owned independent bookshop opened December 2024, selling books, gifts, handmade art and crafts. A second site exists in Romiley (a few miles away, same family) — a genuine small 2-site sibling pair, within the precedent already accepted elsewhere in this file. Coordinates (53.412667/-2.157474) from the SK1 1UD postcode centroid — roughly 250m from the Underbanks/Market Place district centroid itself, comfortably within the district's real footprint alongside its other venues. Reuses the existing BOOKSHOP type (Simply Books, Chorlton Bookshop). Stockport (Underbanks)'s Do category (Stockport Market Hall, Staircase House, two art galleries) had no bookshop before this addition. High confidence — recently opened, well-documented, no closure signals.

suggestions.name: Chapel Holistics
suggestions.reason: An award-winning holistic retreat tucked into The Precinct — facials and massage at the unhurried pace of somewhere that's never had to chase footfall.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via Stockport Mumbler, the operator's own site (chapelholisticsltd.co.uk) and Tripadvisor (active reviews): Chapel Holistics Beauty Retreat, 21c The Precinct, Cheadle Hulme SK8 5BB — a multi-award-winning independent beauty salon and holistic retreat offering facials, massage and complementary therapies. No second site found anywhere in searches; single-site, passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Coordinates from the SK8 5BB postcode centroid. Reuses the existing SPA type (Base & Boon, Hale Country Club & Spa). Cheadle Hulme had zero Do-category wellness/spa venue before this addition. High confidence — well-documented, no closure signals.

suggestions.name: Saul Hay Gallery
suggestions.reason: A railway cottage behind the old Bass Warehouse, hung with contemporary painting and sculpture nobody's pitching as an investment — Castlefield's actual private-dealer gallery.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via the gallery's own site (saulhayfineart.co.uk), Tripadvisor and Yelp (both active 2026 listings): Saul Hay Gallery, Railway Cottage, Castle Street, Manchester M3 4LZ, a contemporary art gallery a few minutes' walk from Deansgate-Castlefield tram station, selling original paintings, sculpture and limited-edition prints. No second site found anywhere in searches; single-site, independently owned, passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Coordinates (53.474461/-2.254742) from the M3 4LZ postcode centroid, within the Deansgate ward per the same source. Reuses the existing ART GALLERY type. Deansgate's Do category was its thinnest alongside Drink and Eat (4 each) before this addition — no venue there currently offers a gallery visit. High confidence — long-established, well-documented, no closure signals. Checked against docs/data/venues.json before writing this: not a duplicate of The Horsfall (Ancoats, already live) or any other existing gallery entry.

suggestions.name: Next Door Gallery
suggestions.reason: A family fine-art publisher's own retail gallery on Burton Road, forty years in the trade before they hung a show under their own name — local and UK/European artists priced to actually buy, not just admire.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via the gallery's own site (thegallerynextdoor.co.uk), Companies House (THE GALLERY NEXT DOOR LTD, #13465607, active, incorporated 2021), Facebook and creativetourist.com: Next Door Gallery, 238 Burton Road, West Didsbury, Manchester M20 2LW — a retail gallery run by a family fine-art publishing business with 40+ years in the trade, showing and selling original paintings, prints and sculpture from local and wider UK/European artists. No second site found anywhere in searches; single-site, passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Coordinates from the M20 2LW postcode centroid (doogal.co.uk). Reuses the existing ART GALLERY type. Didsbury's Do category was its thinnest before this addition (2 real Do-mapped venues — Fletcher Moss Botanical Garden, Marie Louise Gardens — Sett174 Art Cafe's ART STUDIO type isn't currently wired into CATEGORY_BY_VENUE_TYPE). High confidence — established, well-documented, no closure signals.

suggestions.name: Siamease Thai Spa
suggestions.reason: Five treatment rooms above Faulkner Street, run by therapists trained the traditional way in Thailand since 2013 — Chinatown's actual quiet hour, one flight up from the karaoke and the dim sum queue.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via the operator's own site (siamease.co.uk), Tripadvisor and Treatwell (both active 2026 listings with recent reviews): Siamease Thai Spa, 48 Faulkner Street, Manchester M1 4FH, Chinatown — founded by Sally in 2013, Thai-trained therapists, 5 treatment rooms, open daily. No second site found anywhere in searches; single-site, passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Coordinates from the M1 4FH postcode centroid (doogal.co.uk). Reuses the existing SPA type. Deliberately not the same venue as the already-rejected Bali Health Lounge (dissolved, see this file's own record) — a different address, operator and company. Chinatown's Do category (3 real venues, all art galleries — Contemporary Six, Manchester Art Gallery, T.La Art & Craft) had no spa/wellness variety before this addition. Moderate-high confidence — long-established (12+ years trading), well-documented; reviews are mixed on service consistency but show no closure signal.

suggestions.name: Tempranillo
suggestions.reason: Spanish tapas and sherry in a cobbled Back Wallgate cottage that's been pouring Rioja since long before small plates were a trend anywhere else in town.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via the operator's own site (tempranillobar.co.uk), CAMRA's own pub listing, OpenTable and the Food Standards Agency ratings register: Tempranillo, 17 Back Wallgate, Macclesfield SK11 6LQ — a long-established independent Spanish wine and tapas bar in a historic cobbled-street building. No second site or group ownership found anywhere in searches; single-site, passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Coordinates from the SK11 6LQ postcode centroid (doogal.co.uk). Reuses the existing SMALL PLATES type (Shrub, Bar San Juan). Closes Macclesfield's most acute real gap this run: only 1 category-mapped Eat venue (Amazing India — BeefnBerry Bistro and Chestergate Bistro's BISTRO type isn't wired into CATEGORY_BY_VENUE_TYPE) against 4 Do and 4 Drink venues before this addition. Moderate-high confidence — long-established and well-documented across multiple independent sources; reviews are mixed on service consistency on any given night but show no closure signal.

suggestions.name: The Bottle Stop
suggestions.reason: An independent bottle shop on Acre Lane stocked deeper in Belgian and German imports than anywhere else nearby bothers with — a couple of taps out front for whoever can't wait to get home to open one.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via Facebook (@thebottlestopbramhall, active), Yelp/ratebeer/Wheree listings (consistent current details) and the venue's own contact number: The Bottle Stop, 136 Acre Lane, SK8 7PD — an independent wine, beer and spirits shop with a couple of beer taps to drink in or take away. No second site or group ownership found anywhere in searches; single-site, passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. High confidence — well-established, well-documented, no closure signals.

suggestions.name: Smaak
suggestions.reason: Manchester's first Dutch fry house, tucked down Back Turner Street — Amsterdam-style fries and breakfast buns from a kitchen that's never once tried to be a chip shop.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via themanc.com's own opening coverage, secretmanchester.com, manchestersfinest.com and the operator's own site (smaak.co.uk): Smaak, 42 Back Turner Street, Manchester M4 1FR — billed as Manchester's first Dutch 'Het Friethuis', serving Amsterdam-style fries, breakfast buns, waffles, beers and cocktails; a genuinely new opening (2026). No second site or group ownership found anywhere in searches; single-site, passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Coordinates from the M4 1FR postcode centroid (doogal.co.uk). New type introduced — DUTCH FRY HOUSE — since no existing Eat type captures a dedicated Dutch fries-and-brunch concept precisely (BRUNCH SPOT is the closest fit but would flatten the genuinely distinct Dutch-street-food identity that's the actual reason to go); same precedent as SOUVLAKI SPOT/SMOKEHOUSE/CANTONESE ROAST elsewhere in this catalog. Northern Quarter's Eat category (4 venues: BAB NQ, Evelyn's, Idle Hands, This & That) was its thinnest relative to Do (6) and Drink (7) before this addition. Moderate-high confidence — very recently opened, so less of a review history than an established venue, but well-documented by multiple independent local outlets with no closure signal (there being nothing yet to close).

suggestions.name: Structure Wellness
suggestions.reason: A movement studio off Stevenson Square from a trainer who got tired of gyms that didn't care — reformer, breathwork and a retreat room upstairs, nothing about it franchised.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via ClassPass, Tagvenue's own venue-hire listing and LinkedIn (Sean Boyd, founder): Structure Wellness, 8 Stevenson Square, Manchester, Northern Quarter (M1 1DN postcode area) — a movement and wellbeing studio founded by Sean Boyd in 2021, offering pilates/reformer, breathwork and wellness classes plus a retreat/venue-hire space. No evidence of a second site or franchise structure found anywhere in searches (a separate Lever Street address referenced in some listings appears to be the same studio's alternate/venue-hire entrance, not a second location); single operator, passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Coordinates from the M1 1DN postcode centroid (doogal.co.uk). Reuses the existing WELLNESS STUDIO type (Wilmslow Pilates & Wellness). Closes a real citywide gap, not just a district one: before this addition, Northern Quarter had zero Spa & wellness-tile venue, and the tile itself had only 6 real matches across the whole Manchester/Cheshire catalogue. Moderate-high confidence — well-documented, currently operating; the two-address detail is the one flag worth a second look at promotion time.

suggestions.name: Nichols & Co

suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via the operator's own site (nicholstyle.co.uk), Drapers Online, Facebook and Companies House (NICHOLS & CO (CHESTER) LIMITED): Nichols & Co, 5 Bridge Street Row East, Chester CH1 1NW — an independent lifestyle boutique established 2002, owned and run by Ronnie and Rachael Nichols, spanning three floors of womenswear, jewellery, accessories and homeware from UK/European designers. New type introduced — FASHION BOUTIQUE already exists elsewhere in the catalogue (Beaumont Organic, Northern Quarter; Tuula, Alderley Edge) and is reused here, not new. High confidence — 23+ years of continuous trading, well-documented, no closure signals.

suggestions.name: Egg & Co
suggestions.reason: Started as a stall inside Ancoats General Store before it earned its own address on Deansgate — an egg sandwich taken as seriously as anything with a tasting menu.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via themanc.com's own opening coverage, manchestersfinest.com and the Food Standards Agency ratings register: Egg & Co, 247 Deansgate, Manchester M3 4EN — an egg-sandwich specialist that built its name through residencies at Ancoats General Store, Stretford Foodhall and Kargo (Salford) before opening this, its first standalone bricks-and-mortar restaurant and takeaway. Deansgate's Eat category (Pip, Podium Restaurant, Dimitri's, Another Hand — no brunch-specific venue) gets real variety from this addition rather than another fine-dining room. Moderate-high confidence — well-documented, recently opened, no closure signal; the residency-to-standalone history is the one thing worth re-checking at promotion time.

suggestions.name: Rubber Ducky Records
suggestions.reason: A record shop that lives on a narrowboat moored in Islington Marina — mostly secondhand electronic vinyl, a turntable to test it on before you buy, and a genuine appointment required before you're allowed aboard.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via manchestersfinest.com, The Vinyl Factory, Mixmag, The Northern Quota and GigPig: Rubber Ducky Records, moored at Islington Marina, Ancoats, Manchester (correspondence address 10 Redhill Street, M4 6EY) — a floating, appointment-only secondhand electronic-vinyl record shop that opened October 2022, run by a single owner (Myles), genuinely one-of-a-kind ('the UK's first and only floating record store'). No second site possible or found — passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Coordinates from the M4 6EY postcode centroid (doogal.co.uk), the nearest fixed address to the marina mooring; flagged for the reviewer since a boat's exact position can shift within the marina. Reuses the existing RECORD SHOP type (introduced for the Chicago pass). Suggested with `bookingRequired: true` in mind for promotion — the shop is genuinely appointment-based, a real 'can't walk in without arranging it first' case per CLAUDE.md's Matchmaking contract, not an inferred guess. Ancoats' Do category (Hallé St Peter's, Hope Mill Theatre, The Horsfall, Social Refuge) gets a genuinely distinctive addition rather than more of the same. Moderate confidence — real and well-documented, but the appointment-only/floating nature is unusual enough to warrant the reviewer's own look before promotion.

suggestions.name: The Beauty Barn Mobberley
suggestions.reason: A converted farm building at Owen House, run as both a working salon and its own training academy — the kind of unhurried facial that only makes sense this far outside the city.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via the operator's own site (thebeautybarnmobberley.co.uk), Facebook, Yell and Birdeye (115 reviews, 5-star average): The Beauty Barn Mobberley, Salon & Training Academy, Owen House Farm Offices, Wood Lane, Mobberley WA16 7NY — an independent beauty salon and training academy in converted farm buildings, over 19 years of combined staff experience. Passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Coordinates from the WA16 7NY postcode centroid (doogal.co.uk), roughly 2.3km from the Mobberley district centroid, well within the village's real footprint alongside its other rural venues. Moderate-high confidence — well-documented, long-operating, no closure signals.

suggestions.name: Mobberley Brewhouse Tap & Shop

suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via CAMRA/whatpub.com, Great British Life ('Local life — Mobberley Tap & Shop') and Untappd (check-ins as recent as August 2026, confirming current trading): Mobberley Brewhouse Tap & Shop, Dairy Farm, Church Lane, Mobberley WA16 7RA — the original site of Mobberley Brewhouse, kept running as a taproom and bottle/can shop after brewing production relocated to larger premises on Woodend Lane. Coordinates from the WA16 7RA postcode centroid (web geocode search, doogal.co.uk blocked this session). High confidence on Mobberley Brewhouse itself — small, single-site, well-documented, current 2026 activity confirmed.

suggestions.name: The Spinn Off

Moderate-high confidence — well-documented, currently trading, no closure signals; the Gatley sibling is the one flag worth a second look at promotion time.

suggestions.name: Ōdiobā

suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via Manchester's Finest, The Cheshire Magazine, Taste of Manchester and Tripadvisor (active 2026 listing): Ōdiobā, 26 Lower Hillgate, Stockport SK1 1JE — a hi-fi listening bar and coffee shop opened by the team behind Nam (the listening bar already live in this catalogue under Ancoats), carrying over Nam's original sound system. Same-owner sibling of an already-catalogued venue in a different Manchester-metro district — the precedent already established for Craig's/Ivy Spinningfields, applied here to two districts within the same metro rather than two cities. No third site found for either Nam or Ōdiobā. suggestions.name: The Dulcimer

suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via Manchester Confidential ('Ten years and still a hit: Chorlton's Dulcimer'), CAMRA/whatpub.com and Yelp (active listing with reviews dated September 2026): The Dulcimer, 567 Wilbraham Road, Chorlton-cum-Hardy, Manchester (postcode given inconsistently across sources as M21 4AE/M21 0AE) — opened 2007 in a former art shop, described by The Guardian at the time as 'the hippest new music venue in Manchester', now a long-running independent live-music bar known for folk and folk-crossover programming plus cask ales and craft ciders. Moderate-high confidence — long-established, well-documented, current reviews; the coordinate approximation is the one flag.

Moderate-high confidence — well-documented, current social activity, no closure signals.

suggestions.name: Butter Bird

Ancoats' real Eat category (Erst, Mana, Pollen Bakery, Indian Affair) gets genuine variety from this addition. Moderate-high confidence — very recently opened so less review history than an established venue, but well-documented by multiple independent local outlets with no closure signal.

suggestions.name: The Bubble Room Bramhall

The Monkey Lounge in the back seats forty') confirms the same concept. No third site found anywhere in searches. Closes Bramhall's real Eat gap (Pix Pizza, Amici, Plumcake Cafe) with a genuinely different register — a late-running bar-restaurant rather than another Italian table. High confidence — long-established, well-documented, directly tied to an already-verified sibling.

suggestions.name: Linden Stores
suggestions.reason: Laura Christie and Chris Boustead's third address for the same restaurant — Highbury, then Audlem, now Minshull Street — an AA Rosette earned on a wine list that still changes with whatever they've just found.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via The Caterer, Great British Life ('Meet the chef: Laura Christie and Chris Boustead'), Hardens and Tripadvisor (active 2026 listing, 1 AA Rosette awarded March 2025): Linden Stores, 15 Minshull Street, Knutsford WA16 6HG — a relaxed bistro, wine bar and bottle shop run by chef-owners Laura Christie (ex-Oklava, Kyseri) and Chris Boustead (ex-Opera Tavern). Genuinely a single restaurant that has relocated over time rather than a chain with concurrent sites: launched in Highbury, London in 2017, moved to Audlem, Cheshire in 2021, then to this Knutsford address in November 2023 — only ever one site trading at once. Passes Hard rule 1 cleanly on that basis. Coordinates from the WA16 6HG postcode centroid (web geocode search). Reuses the existing SMALL PLATES type (LI~LY is TASTING MENU, a different register). Knutsford's real Eat category (LI~LY, Giovanni's, Neki, The Stolen Lamb) gets a genuinely distinct small-plates/wine-bar-hybrid addition. High confidence — well-documented history, current AA Rosette, active reviews, no closure signals.
